items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: Everybody was from New Orleans, except for one man, Hiram Hardy.

ctx.x: Whereas your band, unless I knew you were from New Orleans, I would not necessarily have spotted it, maybe Contrell, you know, because you didn't, on the record I'm talking about, you know.

Yeah, that wasn't later, that's after the big arrangements came up. Yes. But at the first plane, which we don't have any records of, in 1929 at the State Fair, nine musicians from New Orleans, you didn't have anything but a New Orleans beat. Yeah. Everybody was from New Orleans, except for one man, Hiram Hardy.
You know, I hear New Orleans fans today still sing this the same way.
Yeah, a lot of times musicians copy things they thought had a catch to it. That gives you Cattrall at his greatest. Yeah. That's Hiram Hardy, Dallas boy.
You know who that is? Yeah. I think she has. Now, let's see what we're doing.
